name: Origin Roasters
tagline: Roasted on Tuesday, shipped on Wednesday. Beans with a farm passport

listing.description: A site for a roastery, a whole-bean shop or a tea brand. A dark, data-rich theme: a live roast profile, lots with a flavour wheel and a subscription shown as coffee bags.

seo.title: Origin Roasters — fresh-roasted coffee in Tashkent
seo.description: A roastery in Chilanzar: specialty beans from Ethiopia, Colombia, Kenya and Brazil, roasted every Tuesday, with a subscription delivered across Uzbekistan and wholesale for cafés.
seo.answer: Origin Roasters is a roastery at 28 Qatortol St in Tashkent. We roast every Tuesday and the shop is open Tuesday to Saturday, 10:00–19:00. A 250 g bag starts at 145,000 UZS and the Two Bags a Month subscription costs 270,000 UZS with delivery across Uzbekistan. Wholesale for cafés starts at 5 kg.

sections.title: Fresh roast every Tuesday
sections.subtitle: We buy green coffee directly from farms, roast it in small 12 kg batches and ship within a day. Every bag carries the farm, altitude, process and roast date.

items.title: Farm
items.text: We choose lots from samples and cupping and buy without middlemen.

items.title: Roast
items.text: Every Tuesday, 12 kg batches, a profile for each lot.

items.title: Cupping
items.text: We cup every batch: what does not pass never reaches a bag.

items.title: Delivery
items.text: Next day in Tashkent, 2–4 days across Uzbekistan.

items.q: How long do the beans keep?
items.a: It tastes best from day 5 to day 30 after roasting. Keep the bag closed and out of the fridge.

items.q: Can you grind for a cezve?
items.a: Yes — for a cezve, pour-over, French press, moka pot or espresso. Just mark it when ordering.

items.q: Do you deliver to the regions?
items.a: Across Uzbekistan in 2–4 days, free on the Two Bags subscription.

items.q: Can I come to a cupping?
items.a: Open cupping every Saturday at 12:00, free, booking required.
Yes: wholesale from 5 kg a week, barista training and equipment setup.
